items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: Oh, he really did impress me. He was so far ahead of his time, he wasn't even funny.

ctx.x: Oh, he really did impress me. He was so far ahead of his time, he wasn't even funny. It was amazing what a tone he...
On the record, even, you can tell the beautiful tone. I just wondered how he was in person. I never heard him.

items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: We used to hire a launch, you know, in Chicago. And he'd go, and they'd get through it to the Friars Inn. We'd hire a launch and go out on the lake. And he'd take the guitar.

ctx.x: He was quite a pure player then. He was? He was really influenced by the piano. Yes. Oh, that shows on his records. On his piano things. Did he write most of his tunes on the piano? Oh, yes. Those are all original. To me, on the piano. No one knows what he really amounted to for your life today. Yeah. No one knows. It might have been greater than him. They'd write about you with body pooped out. I think he'd probably have gone to the piano. You think so? I think so. He would have left his chorus completely. Well,…

Pops, Faust and Muggsy, Spanier, April 21st, 1957, reel three. Did you like the way he played? Oh, yes, I liked the way he played. Did you get together and play a lot together? Oh, yes, we played every night in Chicago. In various clubs? Oh, yes. No, there was a round roll. Oh, there are. Then we'd go out together. We'd go out the south side. And I'd probably go there. We'd sit in there together. I wouldn't care to go. Rap could really play some blues on guitar, couldn't he, Pop? Yeah, that's why I... How good a…

Brown shoes. And the biggest thing that I've seen, we were in the Primal Theater, Louie come downstairs with his tails on, shirt and everything with the pants. And they're blowing his own dress around there. I said, this is where you go on stage. I said, where the hell is your pants? Go to the moon, what the hell you talking about, my brother? That's where you go. How dear to the moon goes to the bamboo
